newsitem.title: ITALY: Parmalat makes $300 million bid for Ault Foods.
newsitem.headline: Parmalat makes $300 million bid for Ault Foods.

text.p: Parmalat, one of Italy's biggest food companies, Monday offered nearly $300 million to buy Canada's Ault Foods, topping a rival hostile takeover bid from another dairy producer, Saputo Group.

In what would be its second acquisition in Canada in four months, Parmalat and its U.S. partner, Citicorp, agreed to pay C$34 ($24.48) for each Ault share, above Saputo's C$28 bid ($20.16), making Parmalat's total bid worth C$415 million ($299 million).
Ault Foods is a leading Canadian producer and distributor of products such as cheese and butter. It has 10 production plants and 1,994 employees.
Parmalat said the acquisition would create a company with annual sales of almost C$2 billion ($1.44 billion) and operating profits of more than C$110 million ($79 million).
In March, Parmalat bought a majority stake in Canada's Beatrice Foods in a deal worth C$290 million ($209 million). In that deal, Parmalat bought 75.1 percent of Beatrice and Citicorp 24.9 percent.
Parmalat said it and Citicorp would raise funds to buy Ault through a jointly owned holding company with other funds coming from a group of banks.
Parmalat stock on the Milan market was temporarily suspended ahead of the announcement, and when it reopened fell sharply to close down 5.98 percent at 2,311 lire ($1.37).
Ault shares rose C$2.20 at C$34.20 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday, above the Parmalat bid price, indicating investors expect that a new, higher bid might emerge.
A Saputo senior executive told Reuters the Montreal-based company would not rule out a higher bid for Ault, but needed access to Ault's books.

"It's possible only if we have access to the books," Saputo Executive Vice President Camillo Lisio said in a telephone interview. "We certainly don't have the privilege of knowing what Parmalat knows about the company."
Closely held Saputo makes dairy products and has interests in real estate and transportation.

Analysts said Parmalat's stock price was weakened with Parmalat making its second major acquisition in four months pushing up company debt, but in the long term this gave Parmalat a strong foothold in North America and expanded its global coverage.

Parmalat said the Ault acquisition would be made through a new company, Parmalat Foods Inc., 100 percent owned by Parmalat Canada Inc., which in turn is 75.1 percent owned by Parmalat and 24.9 percent by Citicorp after the Beatrice deal.

Parmalat added that Ault Foods has a 14 percent share of the Canadian national market in cheese and margarine, 36 percent in butter and some 26 percent of the liquid milk market in the province of Quebec.
